text: Cyclone Akvan hit land, and within hours, it started dying. Why?
On Friday morning it crossed the Odisha coast near Gopalpur, and soon weakened into a deep depression.
A cyclone is a giant engine, and its fuel is warm sea water, above about twenty six degrees.
Warm, wet air rises, cools, and turns into towering clouds.
That releases heat, which sucks in even more air, faster and faster.
But over land, there is no warm sea to drink from. The fuel line is cut.
And trees, hills and buildings drag on the winds, slowing them down.
But it doesn't die quietly. Its leftover clouds still dump heavy rain far inland.
Did Akvan bring rain to your city? Comment yes or no.
